chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'They used to consider that charity wards off [harm] from the greatly wronged/oppressive man.'

key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Voluntary charity (sadaqa) — distinct from obligatory zakat; given freely to earn God's pleasure and ward off harm
key_terms.الظَّلُوم: One who is greatly oppressive or greatly wronged — intensive form of zalim; ambiguous whether it refers to the oppressor or the oppressed, with classical scholars debating both readings
key_terms.تُدْفَعُ: Is repelled/warded off — passive form indicating the charity acts as a barrier against harm

ai.seo_question: Does charity ward off harm and injustice according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) quotes Imam Ali (AS) reporting an established belief among the early Muslim community: that giving charity acts as a shield, repelling calamity and harm even from one who has committed serious wrongs. This teaching reflects the widely held view in Islamic tradition that sadaqa carries a protective spiritual function, capable of averting misfortune and divine punishment. The chain Nawfali-Sakuni is a known pair associated with transmitting Sunni-origin traditions accepted within the Shia corpus.
